summary: Sega AM2's foundational 3D fighting series, covering the Model 1 and Model 2 arcade originals, Saturn-era spin-offs, VF4's arcade-network era, and the modern VF5 R.E.V.O. rollback/crossplay line.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / arcade preservation setup
emulation.notes: Use Saturn emulation only to compare the launch home conversion.

primary.why: The first Virtua Fighter is the original polygonal 3D fighting game and shipped on arcade, Saturn, 32X, R-Zone, and Windows-related releases. For the untouched 1993 game, the arcade Model 1 version is the definitive historical route; Remix and 10th Anniversary are separate enhanced entries.
primary.how_to_play: Play an original arcade cabinet or a legal arcade-preservation setup; use Saturn/32X only for home-port comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Virtua Fighter Remix and Virtua Fighter 10th Anniversary are separate enhanced/remake entries.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter Remix

emulation.notes: Use a legacy Windows VM if modern compatibility is poor.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter Remix updated the original game with textured graphics and shipped on Saturn, arcade, and Windows as Virtua Fighter PC. The Windows release is the most configurable home route for this specific enhanced version.
primary.how_to_play: Play Virtua Fighter PC on a compatible Windows setup or preservation VM; Saturn is a fallback for the same enhanced branch.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is an enhanced version of the first game, not the untouched arcade original.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 2

emulation.emulator: PS3/Xbox 360 entitlement / Model 2 arcade preservation / Mednafen Saturn fallback
emulation.notes: Use the 2012 digital release if owned; otherwise preserve the arcade or Saturn version.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official HD-era digital release or original Model 2 arcade fidelity

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 2 has many ports, including Saturn, Genesis/Mega Drive, Windows, PS2, iOS, PS3, and Xbox 360. The 2012 PS3/Xbox 360 digital releases are the best practical route to the arcade-style game, while the Genesis version is a distinct 2D conversion without the full roster.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 2012 PS3 or Xbox 360 digital release if already owned; otherwise use Saturn or arcade-preservation routes.

secondary.exclusive_content: Distinct 2D remake/conversion that omits Shun and Lion
secondary.what_to_play: Sample a few matches to see the unusual 2D adaptation.
secondary.why: It is not the fidelity route, but it is materially different from the 3D versions.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Genesis/Mega Drive version is a separate 2D adaptation rather than the definitive game.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 2.1

emulation.emulator: PS3/Xbox 360 entitlement / arcade or Saturn preservation
emulation.notes: Prefer the owned 2012 digital release.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 2.1 is the tuned arcade update of Virtua Fighter 2, later represented across Saturn, Windows, PS2, PS3, and Xbox 360 routes. The 2012 PS3/Xbox 360 digital release is the best practical modern route to the tuned version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the 2012 digital release if owned; otherwise use Saturn/Windows/PS2 preservation routes.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a tuned VF2 update, so it is tracked separately from base Virtua Fighter 2.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter CG Portrait Series

emulation.notes: Use disc images from owned copies only.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Saturn output or Saturn emulation

primary.why: Virtua Fighter CG Portrait Series is documented as a Saturn CD series of character pose/viewer discs. It is an archival media/game-adjacent entry rather than a competitive fighting game, and Saturn is the only documented platform.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Saturn discs/hardware or Saturn emulation to view the portrait discs.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a standard fighting-game entry; included for franchise completeness.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter Animation

emulation.notes: Use Master System emulation for capture-friendly play.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter Animation, also known as Virtua Fighter Mini, was released on Game Gear and later Master System. The Master System version is the selected route for a larger-screen home version, while Game Gear is the original handheld route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Master System release on original hardware or through a compatible emulator; use Game Gear for the original handheld version.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter Kids

emulation.notes: Use Saturn emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter Kids is a super-deformed Virtua Fighter spin-off released in arcades and on Saturn. The Saturn version is the practical full-play home route for this spin-off.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Saturn release on original hardware or through Saturn emulation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Fighters Megamix

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or accurate Saturn emulation.

primary.why: Fighters Megamix is a Saturn crossover featuring Virtua Fighter 2 and Fighting Vipers characters, VF3-style movement ideas, and hidden Virtua Fighter-related characters. Saturn is the only documented release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Saturn release on original hardware or through Mednafen Saturn.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: All-Japan Pro Wrestling Featuring Virtua

emulation.notes: Japanese text/menu familiarity may be required.

primary.why: All-Japan Pro Wrestling Featuring Virtua is a Japan-only wrestling game featuring Virtua Fighter characters Jeffry and Wolf alongside Japanese wrestlers. It launched on Saturn and later reached arcades; the Saturn release is the practical home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese Saturn release on original hardware or through Saturn emulation; use the arcade version only for preservation comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 3

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Supermodel-compatible preservation setup
emulation.notes: Use original Model 3 hardware where possible.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 3 launched on Sega Model 3 arcade hardware and introduced Aoi, Taka-Arashi, stage undulation, and the dodge button. The later 3tb update and Dreamcast version are separate entries, so the original arcade version is primary here.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware or a compatible Model 3 preservation setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Virtua Fighter 3tb and 3tb Online are separate update entries.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 3tb

emulation.notes: Use Dreamcast emulation for clean capture and scaling.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 3tb added tournament/team-battle structure and was released in arcades and on Dreamcast. The Dreamcast version is the practical home route for this update; 3tb Online is tracked separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast release on original hardware or through Flycast/Redream; use arcade hardware for cabinet authenticity.

entries.remaster_caveats: Virtua Fighter 3tb Online is a separate modern arcade update.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 4

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and low-latency controller setup.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 4 launched in arcades on NAOMI 2 and received a well-regarded PS2 port with deep training features. Evolution and Final Tuned are separate entries, so the PS2 release is the full home route for base VF4.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware or through PCSX2 with high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Virtua Fighter 4: Evolution and Final Tuned are separate updates.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 4: Evolution

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution; keep save data for Quest progression/customization.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 4: Evolution added Brad and Goh plus balance and Quest-style content, then received a PS2 release. The PS2 version is the best full-play route for this update, and includes the 10th Anniversary remake in some regions/editions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 Evolution release through PCSX2 with high internal resolution; preserve the 10th Anniversary bonus separately if included.

entries.remaster_caveats: Final Tuned is a later arcade-only update and separate entry.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 10th Anniversary

emulation.notes: Use a legitimate copy/edition that includes the bonus.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 10th Anniversary is a PS2 remake of the first game using VF4 Evolution character mechanics while retaining VF1-style music, stages, and low-polygon presentation. It was distributed through Japanese box-set and regional bonus/promo routes, so the PS2 version is the only documented route.
primary.how_to_play: Play from the Japanese 10th Anniversary set or the North American VF4 Evolution bonus on PS2/PCSX2.

entries.remaster_caveats: It is a remake/bonus using later mechanics, not a substitute for the original 1993 arcade game.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 4: Final Tuned

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / NAOMI 2 preservation setup
emulation.notes: Verify compatibility before planning a full route.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 4: Final Tuned is documented as a 2004 arcade-only upgrade to Evolution. No home release is documented, so the arcade version is the only complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware where available; otherwise preserve as an arcade-only update.

entries.remaster_caveats: Arcade-only; use Evolution on PS2 for the closest home version, but it is not the same revision.

entries.title: Virtua Quest

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and widescreen only if compatibility is stable.

primary.why: Virtua Quest is a Virtua Fighter action-RPG spin-off released for GameCube and PS2. With no sourced content split, GameCube is selected as the sharper sixth-generation route, with PS2 as a fallback.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GameCube version on original hardware or through Dolphin with high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 5

emulation.notes: Prefer original Xbox 360 hardware for reliable base VF5 Online play.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 5 launched in arcades and came to PS3 and Xbox 360. The Xbox 360 version added online play, improved graphics, and balance updates from a newer arcade revision, making it the best route for the original VF5 home release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 release if preserving base VF5; use later Final Showdown or R.E.V.O. entries for the modern competitive route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Final Showdown and R.E.V.O. are later update entries with different balance/content.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 5 Online

emulation.notes: Use original hardware for best compatibility.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 5 Online is the Xbox 360 online-enabled VF5 release identified separately in the series timeline. It is the only documented platform for this named version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version for this specific online-enabled release; use modern R.E.V.O. World Stage for active rollback/crossplay.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online infrastructure and account access may limit historical functionality.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 5 R

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Lindbergh preservation setup
emulation.notes: Verify compatibility before planning a full route.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 5 R is an arcade update that returned Taka-Arashi and added Jean Kujo. No home release is documented for the R revision, so arcade is the only complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware where available; use later Final Showdown/R.E.V.O. entries for home access to the broader VF5 update line.

entries.remaster_caveats: Final Showdown supersedes R as a later update but is tracked separately.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter Mobile 3D

emulation.notes: Use a preserved mobile build only.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter Mobile 3D is documented as a 2008 J2ME mobile Virtua Fighter release. No other platform route is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved J2ME phone build or compatible Java mobile preservation setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 5 Final Showdown
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox 360 Final Showdown via backward-compatible Xbox hardware

emulation.emulator: Xbox backward compatibility / PS3 hardware / Xenia/RPCS3 experimental
emulation.notes: Prefer official Xbox backward compatibility if entitlement is available.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD console output or backward-compatible Xbox playback

primary.platform: Xbox 360 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S
primary.version: Final Showdown downloadable release via backward compatibility
primary.why: Final Showdown is the 2010 arcade update that came to PS3 and Xbox 360 in 2012, with later Xbox backward-compatible routes. The Xbox backward-compatible path is the best practical way to play this specific pre-Ultimate-Showdown revision on modern hardware.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 Final Showdown entitlement on Xbox 360, Xbox One, or Xbox Series X|S where available; PS3 is a fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: Ultimate Showdown/R.E.V.O. is a later remake/update line and separate entry.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter: Cool Champ

emulation.notes: Service availability may prevent normal play.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter: Cool Champ is documented as a 2011 mobile Virtua Fighter title. No additional public platform route is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved mobile build/account if available; otherwise treat as a mobile-service preservation entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter: Fever Combo

emulation.notes: Service availability may prevent normal play.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter: Fever Combo is documented as a 2014 mobile Virtua Fighter title. No additional platform route is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved mobile build/account if available; otherwise treat as a mobile-service preservation entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 5 Ultimate Showdown / R.E.V.O. World Stage
entries.definitive_edition: Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage on Windows with DLC

emulation.notes: Use native Windows for fidelity and modern online; install DLC if completeness matters.

primary.version: Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage with DLC
primary.why: Ultimate Showdown rebuilt Final Showdown with Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio visuals on PS4/arcade, while R.E.V.O. brought the update to Windows with 4K support and rollback netcode; World Stage added the single-player campaign, crossplay, and later PS5/Xbox Series/Switch 2 routes. Windows World Stage with DLC installed is the highest-fidelity and most complete current route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage on Windows with the World Stage update and desired DLC installed; PS5/Xbox Series X|S/Switch 2 are excellent crossplay alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: Ultimate Showdown is not the final current version; use R.E.V.O. World Stage for rollback/crossplay and campaign additions.

entries.title: Virtua Fighter 3tb Online

emulation.notes: No home emulation route exists.

primary.why: Virtua Fighter 3tb Online is a 2023 arcade update of Virtua Fighter 3tb. No home release is documented, so arcade is the only sourced route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on supported Japanese arcade hardware/network cabinets where available; otherwise preserve as arcade-only.

entries.remaster_caveats: No home port exists.

primary.why: The new Virtua Fighter project has been announced but is not released yet, and final platforms/version details remain subject to change. This remains a needs-research exception until launch details are stable.
primary.how_to_play: No playable release route yet; revisit after official launch/platform confirmation.
